title: Gravity Pulls Objects Down
seo_title: Grade 5 Gravity Worksheets: Which Way Is Down, Weight and Falling Objects
standard_text: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on gravity (NGSS 5-PS2-1): Earth's gravity pulls toward its center, down on a globe, weight, falling objects and air resistance. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Earth's gravity pulls every object toward Earth's center.
key_sub: Down means toward Earth's center, everywhere on the globe. Gravity pulls without touching and gives objects their weight.
body_html:
How to think about it

Gravity is a force that pulls objects toward Earth. It pulls from a distance: nothing has to touch the object. Gravity gives objects their weight and makes them fall, roll downhill and come back down when thrown.

Earth is a sphere, and gravity pulls everything toward its center. That is what “down” means. So people all around the world stand on the ground and objects fall toward their feet.

Example

A person at the South Pole drops a ball. In a picture with the South Pole at the bottom, which way does it fall?

Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth.

From the South Pole, the center is up the page.

Answer: Toward Earth's center (up the page).

Example

A feather and a coin are dropped on the Moon. Which lands first?

The Moon has gravity but no air.

No air means nothing slows the feather.

Answer: They land at the same time.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking down means the bottom of the page or map. Down means toward Earth's center.
  • Thinking gravity needs air or only works on falling things. It works everywhere, even on objects at rest.
  • Thinking heavier objects always fall much faster. Differences come from air resistance.
  • Thinking people on the other side of Earth would fall off.

faq.a: Earth's gravity pulls objects toward the center of Earth. That direction is “down,” wherever you are on the globe.

faq.q: Why don't people on the other side of Earth fall off?
faq.a: Gravity pulls them toward Earth's center, which is down for them too.
No. Gravity works in empty space. Objects fall on the Moon, which has no air.
Without air, all objects fall at the same rate. With air, light, wide objects like feathers are slowed down more.

items.q: Which word describes the pull of gravity on an object?

items.q: Why do rivers flow downhill?

Water is attracted to the ocean.
items.e: Water moves to lower places because gravity pulls it.

Earth's gravity pulling the apples down
